mode.description: Network isolation mode: "open" (unrestricted), "restricted" (internet only, no LAN), or "allowlist" (explicit domain list only)

block_private_networks.description: Block access to RFC 1918 private network ranges

block_metadata_endpoint.description: Block access to cloud instance metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254)

allowed_domains.description: Destinations allowed when mode is "allowlist". Accepts exact hostnames ("api.anthropic.com"), raw IPv4 addresses ("8.8.8.8") and IPv4 CIDRs ("10.0.0.0/8"). COI resolves each hostname on the host, installs the addresses in the firewall, and writes the same addresses into the container's /etc/hosts; DNS egress is then blocked, so the container cannot reach an address the firewall was not given. Wildcards are NOT supported and are rejected: with names resolved up front there is no answer to write for a subdomain nobody has asked for yet. List exact hostnames, or the provider's published IP ranges as CIDRs. RFC 1918 ranges are always blocked in allowlist mode.

refresh_interval_minutes.description: How often to re-resolve allowlisted domains to refresh their firewall entries (minutes). This is a safety net: the DNS proxy already installs addresses as the container resolves them.

allow_local_network_access.description: Allow established connections from the entire local network, not just the gateway

use_sudo.description: Whether COI may invoke sudo for network operations (nft/iptables). Defaults to true. Set false to decline passwordless sudo: restricted/allowlist modes then error out (no silent downgrade) and only "open" mode works.
